Introduction
INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS

The power sector reforms in the state of Haryana were initiated by the Government of Haryana (GoH)
under the Haryana Reforms Act 1998 on 10th March 1998. The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission

(HERC) was formed on 16th August 1998 and the Haryana State Electricity Board (HSEB) was unbundled
in to two independent company‟s viz. Haryana Power Generation Corporation Limited (HPGCL), to undertake
generation of electricity, and Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited (HVPNL) to undertake transmission,
distribution and retail supply of electricity in the state of Haryana.

Subsequently in July 1999, two distribution companies viz. Uttar Haryana BijliVitran Nigam Ltd. (UHBVNL)
and Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. (DHBVNL) were separated from HVPNL to exclusively
undertake function of distribution and retail supply of electricity in their respective geographic areas.

Detailed specifications are as under:
2.1 Complaint Handling System (CHS)

CHS shall act as a single central system for all interactions with the consumers for their complaints and queries. It
shall have all possible modes for consumer interaction inbuilt into the system including on-call, web portal, SMS,
WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter, chatbot, email etc.

2.1.1.
Unified Omni-channel communication
i. Phone call through IVRS – IVRS solution, CTI and APIs for integration will be provided by Call center vendor of

DHBVN. Bidder shall be responsible for integrating with existing & future IVRS and CTI. Customers will be able
to directly register their complaints without any human intervention through computerized IVRS. The unique
complaint number will be immediately given to the caller by the IVRS, followed by confirmation through SMS/
WhatsApp. Various services which IVRS can offer includes but not limited to are as follows:
 Get the bill information
 Get the status of last complaint
 check the outage information based on consumer account no & registered mobile number
ii. WhatsApp and SMS – Customer can register complaints and check status using SMS and WhatsApp. Bidder

shall define short codes for various services and consumer can send a defined messaged using short codes to
register complaints and get enquires. SMS and WhatsApp Gateway shall be provided by DHBVN. There
should be provision to broadcast predefined and prescheduled messages to consumers.
iii. DHBVN website- bidder shall design and develop a portal for complaint registration and enquiries related to

power supply, billing, metering etc. In case any payment is to be taken, option should be there to redirect
consumer to the DHBVN‟s existing payment portal. Link of this portal shall be provided on the official website
of DHBVN. This portal will replace existing CGRS portal.
iv. Call Center Agents – Call center agents shall have access to CHS to register complaints & enquires. Agent

shall forward the same to the respective field staff/sub-division of DHBVN for resolution (as per the complaint
handling process defined by DHBVN & subject to amendment from time to time). The latest status of all the
registered complaints should also be available on the IVRS.
v. Decentralized Bijli Suvidha Kendras (BSKs) – DHBVN has Circle/Town Level BSKs where consumers can also
lodge complaints in central CRM.
vi. Email - Customer can lodge its complaint using designated email address. Email shall be integrated with the

CRM. All emails on the given email ID should be available in the CHS and there should be provision of replying
to the emails directly from the CHS. DHBVN shall provide email exchange and email id.
vii. Missed call: CHS shall be integrated with Telephony system of Call center vendor via CTI. All the missed and

dropped calls shall be forwarded to the CHS and CHS should show the list of such call received so that agent
can call those numbers. Once the agent records the complaint against the missed number that should be
removed from the list of the calls to be made by agent. As soon as missed call / dropped call information is
received in CHS, a SMS/ WhatsApp should be sent to consumer detailing multiple modes of complaint
registration and assuring that an agent will call back as soon as possible.

2.1.3.
Scheduler

Soon after the registration of the complaints, the scheduler module will manage the life cycle of the complaint till
closure. It is envisaged to be the back bone of the system and shall control the flow of the complaints to resolution
teams by assigning complaints to the concerned team. Scheduler will create task/to-do list for the customer care
agents like to inform the FRT, take confirmation about attending the complaint, follow up call for the monitoring
purpose of resolution of complaints within the time frame. Scheduler will create list for automated calls of the closed
complaints and transfer the list to telephony system of customer care vendor via CTI which will make automated
outbound call to take feedback from consumer. Scheduler will also create a task/to-do list for the calls to be made to
the consumers who have reported dissatisfaction with the resolution of their complaints.
Following process will generally be followed


As soon as complaint is registered, FRT and JE will be informed through SMS/Notification. System will also
schedule the follow up to inform the FRT about the complaint and take confirmation about attending the
complaint.
Note: - For different categories/sub-categories of complaint or nature of fault the escalation matrix shall be
configurable.


In case the complaint is registered but the FRT or JE or AE details are not available, system shall schedule a
call to the concerned officers to get the required details.


As soon as the FRT details are available, complaints shall be allocated to FRT. In case, the FRT details are
not available, the complaints shall be allocated to the JE


Auto schedule follow up call to FRT / JE/AE after scheduled time


Auto schedule for follow up from the consumers for taking the feedback from the consumers


Area outage follow ups, in case of delay in restoration consumer shall be intimated timely

Scheduler shall ensure that feedbacks are taken timely and prompt actions are being taken. Scheduler shall be
linked to the notification builder to schedule and send the notifications (SMS/email/mobile notification)

2.1.5.
Contextual analytics for complaints management

As the complaints related to power distribution have a context associated with them and without the context
analysis, lot of irrelevant complaints can be registered. For example, if there is an area shutdown due to
breakdown at the 33 or higher KV levels, a single fault will impact thousands of consumers and all complaints
should be combined to reduce duplication of the complaints. System shall intelligently identify such faults,
schedule the confirmation and shall allow combining of the complaints into a single complaint but still should
maintain individual ticket.

2.1.6.
Enquiry module

It is proposed that to access the effectiveness of the software as well as the customer care center operations,
all the interaction with the consumers shall be registered in the system. There shall be a module of the
enquiry where call center agents can register the consumer enquiries and interactions which are not
registered as a complaint. It shall be integrated to billing system to provide real time status to consumers.
System shall have provision to define multiple categories of enquiry.

2.1.7.
Complaints Re-opening provision

Provision for re-opening the complaints on basis of consumer feedback or based on DHBVN‟s requirement.
Re-opened complaints will be examined, the feedback will be collected by the customer care center and
forwarded to the higher officers.

2.1.8.
Tripping/ Breakdown portal

A portal shall be developed to record all information regarding scheduled maintenance and shut downs at
the feeder or sub-station level so that consumer can be provided with appropriate information when they
call for outage related complaints. Primarily it shall be used by circle control room for entering the data.
The system shall also be integrated with RTDAS to capture feeder ON/ OFF status and generate alerts.
APIs for RTDAS integration shall be provided by DHBVN. Based on the level & area affected of
tripping/breakdown/fault the intimation shall also be given to the officers of DHBVN via
SMS/WhatsApp/Automatic outbound call.
In addition, the intimation shall also be broadcasted to pre-defined numbers of various RWAs, Public
Administration, Public representatives, eminent citizens etc. of that area. Regular update on the status of
breakdown/fault along with estimated time shall also be broadcasted.

2.1.9.
Officer portals and mobile apps

CHS should have Role based Mobile apps and web portal access for the officers where they can view the
pending complaints and take action on that. All the reports and real time dashboards shall be available on
both web portals and mobile app. DHBVN is in process of developing its common Mobile app for consumer
and officers under a separate project, in such case the proposed Mobile App as per this RFP may be
discontinued and bidder shall develop APIs to integrate with Proposed common Mobile App as and when it is
ready
2.2. Fault Management
Fault management module will be a backend module for CHS. It will be responsible for recording all the faults

and mapping the different type of complaints with the faults. This will be integrated with Field tracking system
for timely resolution. Key features of this module are:


Real time status of feeder or substation outage related complaints with color coding based on time
lines for the call center and BSK.


Consumer complaints shall to be grouped and tagged to a fault (if DT, 11 kV or 33 kV fault).


Defining the faults types and sub-types and linking them with complaints types and sub-types.
Complaint from consumer can be supply related and fault management system will define whether it is
fuse off, under-ground cable, over-head cable, Pole broken, conductor snapping, distribution
transformer related fault.


Grouping of multiple complaints which are related to single fault or shut-down


If the complaint flow from certain area is higher than the average call flow from that area or if the
complaints from the area exceeds a predefined threshold, matter should be escalated to the
concerning JE


Generate reports of frequent failure points.
The fault management system shall record following information:


Fault type: LT/11kV/33kV/ DT/ 33kV Substation


Fault Details


Restoration Time


% variation in Actual and Allowable Time Limit


Reason for Time variation


Whether fault rectification done with temporary restoration


Works are required for permanent restoration (Pole replacement, Under-ground cable fault rectification
etc.)
2.3. Consumer Feedback Module
Provision to collect the feedback of all registered complaints. System shall be configurable as per the

requirement such that either automatic or manual feedback shall be taken. In case of automatic feedback, bidder
shall provision automatic outbound call & get feedback via IVRS, SMS or WhatsApp. Customer shall be able to
give the feedback by pressing the keys on his/ her mobile. The proposed system shall be able to record all
feedbacks from telephony. There should be a provision to broadcast voice message related to billing, general
awareness etc to consumer via IVRS system as per requirement.

instances are detected, they shall be seamlessly replaced when the traffic is automatically redistributed to servers that

2.11.4 Fail Over Solutions

High availability architecture shall consists of a set of loosely coupled servers which have failover capabilities. Failover
system shall be available in which the functions of a system component shall work as secondary system in the event
that the primary one goes offline, either due to failure or planned down time. A “hot failover‟ shall be supported in which
when all the servers are running simultaneously (primary and secondary) and the load is directed entirely towards a
single server at any given time.

Test Plan

Test plans are prepared for each phase of testing. The initial test plan is created during the Project
Planning phase. The initial test plan describes who performs which type of testing and when. Ideally
master test plan covers all types of test i.e. from unit testing to production testing. The Bidder is expected
to submit the test plans to Utility for approval. Any changes made to the test plan during the project life
cycle should be communicated to UTILITY for approval.
Test plans contains following items:
Roles and responsibilities of test team

o
Approach to testing

o
Function testing

o
User Interface and reports testing

o
Test Scenarios along with entry and exit criteria Test specifications
Test scenarios

Bidder should prepare test scenario for each business scenario. A test scenario when executed should
fulfill a business requirement as per the scope of business functionality. Test scenarios include following:

Test Specification - During the test specification phase, the test cases are specified. It consists of
description of the input, process to be executed and a prediction of output results.
Test Environment - Component developer does unit testing and integration testing. Integration
testing can be delegated to a specialized testing group. Each of the members in the testing group
is provided with testing environment according to his/her role and responsibilities. Following is
sample testing environment for testing:

o
A workstation

o
A set of tools and applications required on workstation like access to user interface,
browser etc.

o
Access to centralized document database (where all the project related documents are
maintained)

o
Access to testing tools and defect logging tools

o
Access to the central database or repository for development and unit testing (this
database contains sample test data)

o
Access to deployed components

Test Data - Test data is prepared for testing at each stage. The test data should be prepared in
such a way that it covers basic path and every alternate path of the code. The basic path and
alternate paths are prioritized to capture relevant data. Tools can also be used to generate test
data.
Test Execution

The following testing steps are usually employed in the project lifecycle. The Lead Partner along with
consortium partners is expected to follow these steps.

Unit Testing - In unit testing, each piece of code has to be rigorously tested. At this stage testing
is done according to the priority of path of code. All the test results are logged in the defect
logging tools. After every the completion of testing, code is corrected for defect logs. This process
is iterative till criteria for successful testing is reached.
Integration Testing - Upon completion of unit testing, integration testing begins. The purpose is to
ensure distinct components of the application still work in accordance to customer requirements.
Test sets will be developed with the express purpose of exercising the interfaces between the
components. This activity is to be carried out by the Test Team. Integration test will be termed
complete when actual results and expected results are either in line or differences are
explainable/acceptable based on client input.
Incremental Integration Testing - Continuous testing of an application as new functionality is
added.

System Testing - System testing is performed when all the components are delivered to central
repository prior to the release of the software. The testing is done on priority basis of business
processes. All the defects are logged and assigned to respective component owners. The
component and unit testing is performed after the correction of code. However, it may depend on
size and type of individual test specifications. Impact analysis is useful to narrow done testing
efforts by identifying critical test cases affected due to code change.

Acceptance Testing – During the test scenarios definition, for each of the business scenario, an
acceptance criterion is defined. Acceptance criteria include expected behavior of the s/w
component and the expected results (data). Expected results form a part of the Exit Criteria. In
addition to expected result and behaviors, some conditions are also specified in the exit criteria.
They can be:

o
Number of bugs to be discovered for a functional module. This depends on size of the
functionality and is an indicator of amount of testing done.

o
If any medium or low-priority errors are outstanding - the implementation risk must be
signed off as acceptable by UTILITY and Lead Partner along with consortium partners

o
All High Priority errors from System Test must be fixed and tested

Bidder needs to get the acceptance criteria approved from UTILITY for all the functional
components of the system. The Acceptance Criteria for each release into production environment

will be agreed upon by Bidder and UTILITY prior to release from Testing to production
environment. After installation, if any bug is reported or there is non-compliance to requirements
then a proper procedure should be followed. End-user should report (“Change Request”) to
his/her supervisor about the bug that will in turn get forwarded to Project Manager (PM). PM will
forward the List of change request to Lead Partner along with consortium partners. After the bug
is fixed, it should be reflected in the production copy after testing it.
Bidder should note that UTILITY can appoint a third party agency for conducting any part of above
testing procedures (in addition to the testing carried out by the bidder).

V = A / B * 100

Force Majeure means any circumstances beyond the control of the parties including:

War and other hostilities, (whether war be declared or not), invasion, act of foreign enemies,
mobilization, requisition or embargo;
b)
c)

d)

e)

15.2 Effect of Force Majeure.

extent that performance of such obligations is prevented by any circumstances of Force Majeure which
